cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Make It Their Idea
cards.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You put those chess pieces in separate trays so confidently. Sorting the club cupboard could be your chance to choose the best set for yourself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: These are biscuits. The chess sets are in the black cases.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Refreshments first. You could choose a black case once you've sorted the others.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cases are identical. I'd do it if I could choose who I play next week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, choose the opponent, not the case. You sort the cupboard and name your opponent; I'll take whoever's left.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 names copied confidence and A3 covers biscuit/chess confusion, but confusing loose biscuits with chessmen strains observable logic.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 biscuit reveal corrects the copied cue; B4 identical cases yields a real desired reward in A5.

relationship.evidence: B4 task-for-opponent bargain is credible but the first mistake feels manufactured.

heightening.evidence: A5 improves the reward but claims control of club pairing without establishing it.

specificity.evidence: A1/A3 trays/cases need no staging, yet recognizable biscuits as pieces is an arbitrary mistake.

brevityWit.evidence: A1 so-confidently declaration explains the Stance more than shows the copied action.
